## Structure and components

- [statement] The authors report that secondary and exploratory clinical outcomes showed improvement or stability, including improvement in the MDS-UPDRS Part III OFF scores by an average of 23 points in the high-dose cohort, in this open-label early-phase trial. (low confidence) — https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-025-08845-y · keywords: Dopaminergic cell replacement: bemdaneprocel and iPSC-derived neurons

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] The authors report an open-label phase I trial (NCT04802733) of bemdaneprocel, an investigational cryopreserved, off-the-shelf dopaminergic neuron progenitor cell product derived from human embryonic stem (hES) cells and grafted bilaterally into the putamen of patients with Parkinson's disease; the registry lists the same study as a Phase 1 study of a human embryonic stem cell-derived midbrain dopamine neuron cell therapy. (medium confidence) — https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-025-08845-y · keywords: Dopaminergic cell replacement: bemdaneprocel and iPSC-derived neurons · also: https://clinicaltrials.gov/api/v2/studies/NCT04802733
- [statement] In the Kyoto University Hospital phase I/II trial of seven patients who received iPS-cell-derived dopaminergic progenitors, the authors report that among six patients subjected to efficacy evaluation, four showed improvements in the Movement Disorder Society Unified Parkinson’s Disease Rating Scale part III OFF score and five showed improvements in the ON scores. (medium confidence) — https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-025-08700-0 · keywords: Dopaminergic cell replacement: bemdaneprocel and iPSC-derived neurons · also: https://www.michaeljfox.org/news/stem-cell-therapy-parkinsons-given-limited-approval-japan
- [statement] The registry describes exPDite-2 as a Phase 3 multicenter, randomized, sham surgery-controlled, double-blind study in approximately 102 adults with Parkinson's disease, with participants randomized in a 2:1 ratio to receive bemdaneprocel or undergo sham surgery. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-02) — https://clinicaltrials.gov/api/v2/studies/NCT06944522 · keywords: Dopaminergic cell replacement: bemdaneprocel and iPSC-derived neurons · also: https://www.neurology.org/doi/10.1212/WNL.0000000000216472

## Facts and statements

- [statement] In the bemdaneprocel phase I trial, twelve patients were enrolled sequentially in a low-dose cohort of 0.9 million cells and a high-dose cohort of 2.7 million cells, and all of the participants received one year of immunosuppression. (medium confidence) — https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-025-08845-y · keywords: Dopaminergic cell replacement: bemdaneprocel and iPSC-derived neurons · also: https://clinicaltrials.gov/api/v2/studies/NCT04802733
- [statement] The authors report that the phase I trial of bemdaneprocel achieved its primary objectives of safety and tolerability one year after transplantation, with no adverse events related to the cell product; an abstract authored by sponsor employees describes the early-phase study as having demonstrated bemdaneprocel was generally safe and well tolerated. (medium confidence) — https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-025-08845-y · keywords: Dopaminergic cell replacement: bemdaneprocel and iPSC-derived neurons · also: https://www.neurology.org/doi/10.1212/WNL.0000000000216472
- [statement] The authors report that at 18 months after grafting putaminal 18Fluoro-DOPA positron emission tomography uptake increased, which they interpret as indicating graft survival. (low confidence) — https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-025-08845-y · keywords: Dopaminergic cell replacement: bemdaneprocel and iPSC-derived neurons
- [statement] The bemdaneprocel authors caution that their data need to be interpreted cautiously in view of the open-label study design, the small patient cohort, the relatively short observation period, the expected fluctuations in PD symptoms and the possibility of placebo effects; the registry lists the study as a single group with no masking. (medium confidence) — https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-025-08845-y · keywords: Dopaminergic cell replacement: bemdaneprocel and iPSC-derived neurons · also: https://clinicaltrials.gov/api/v2/studies/NCT04802733
- [statement] The Kyoto authors state that, as an open-label trial without a control group, the influence of the placebo effect and observer bias must be considered, and that the findings of this single-centre, small-sample trial should be confirmed in multi-centre, large-sample trials with appropriate controls. (low confidence) — https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-025-08700-0 · keywords: Dopaminergic cell replacement: bemdaneprocel and iPSC-derived neurons
- [statement] In STEM-PD, a phase 1/2, open-label, multicenter trial of a cryopreserved, off-the-shelf dopaminergic progenitor product derived from human pluripotent stem cells, the authors report no serious adverse events attributed to the cell product, no graft-induced dyskinesias and no evidence of tumor formation on serial magnetic resonance imaging. (low confidence) — https://www.nature.com/articles/s41591-026-04525-0 · keywords: Dopaminergic cell replacement: bemdaneprocel and iPSC-derived neurons
- [statement] In STEM-PD, seven participants completed 12-month follow-up and one participant died from a pulmonary infection, and the authors state that risks were primarily associated with the immunosuppression regimen. (low confidence) — https://www.nature.com/articles/s41591-026-04525-0 · keywords: Dopaminergic cell replacement: bemdaneprocel and iPSC-derived neurons
- [statement] The registry record lists exPDite-2 as RECRUITING with an estimated primary completion date of 2028-10, and the sponsor-authored abstract states that the first participant was randomized and underwent surgery in August 2025. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-02) — https://clinicaltrials.gov/api/v2/studies/NCT06944522 · keywords: Dopaminergic cell replacement: bemdaneprocel and iPSC-derived neurons · also: https://www.neurology.org/doi/10.1212/WNL.0000000000216472
- [statement] Sumitomo Pharma announced that, as of March 6, 2026, it obtained conditional and time-limited approval in Japan for the allogeneic iPS cell-derived dopaminergic neural progenitor cell product AMCHEPRY (INN: raguneprocel). (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-03-11) — https://www.sumitomo-pharma.com/news/20260306.html · keywords: Dopaminergic cell replacement: bemdaneprocel and iPSC-derived neurons · also: https://www.michaeljfox.org/news/stem-cell-therapy-parkinsons-given-limited-approval-japan

## Research summary — Dopaminergic cell replacement: bemdaneprocel and iPSC-derived neurons

Cell replacement for Parkinson's disease transplants dopaminergic progenitor cells derived from embryonic or induced pluripotent stem cells. Recent early-phase, open-label trials of an embryonic stem cell product and an induced pluripotent stem cell product report safety findings plus exploratory motor and imaging changes, and their authors caution about small cohorts, the absence of a control group and placebo effects. In one trial the authors state that risks were primarily associated with the immunosuppression regimen. A randomized, sham surgery-controlled phase three trial of the embryonic stem cell product is registered as recruiting, and a sponsor announced a conditional, time-limited approval in Japan of an induced pluripotent stem cell product.
